Upon completion of HW_1_Human_Review, either Human_Worker_Pressed_Green_Button or Human_Worker_Pressed_Red_Button happens depending on what the button color the human presses.
Trace 102 starts with the event HBW_2_Unload as only start event.
The event HBW_1_Get_Empty_Bucket is executed in parallel to VGR_1_Pick_Up_and_Transport_Run2. After both events are completed, the event VGR_1_Pick_Up_And_Transport_Run3 is executed.
SM_2_Transport fails if there is a loud noise above approximately 90 decibels.
If the sensor value capturing the pressure is above something like 0.48 bar, WT_2_Pick_Up_And_Transport will wear 1.5 times faster.
The event VGR_1_Pick_Up_And_Transport is executed after the event DM_2_Lower.
Before HBW_1_Store is executed VGR_1_Pick_Up_And_Transport_Run3 is completed.
The events VGR_2_Pick_Up_And_Transport and HBW_2_Store_Empty_Bucket are executed in parallel. Afterwards, OV_2_Burn is executed.
The event HW_1_Human_Review has a uniform distribution with a minimum of 2 minutes 3 seconds and maximum of 5 minutes 56 seconds.
After HBW_2_Unload, the events VGR_2_Pick_Up_And_Transport and HBW_2_Store_Empty_Bucket are executed in parallel.
Every 50000 executions of VGR_2_Pick_Up_And_Transport the battery needs to be changed.
With a probability of 70% Human_Worker_Pressed_Green_Button is executed.
After Human_Worker_Pressed_Green_Button or Human_Worker_Pressed_Red_Button, the events HBW_1_Get_Empty_Bucket AND VGR_1_Pick_Up_And_Transport_Run2 are executed in parallel.
If the sensor value for the vibration is equal or higher than 7.1, WT_2_Pick_Up_And_Transport will fail immediately.
The process end is a direct successor of HBW_1_Store.
After Cell1 fails, the repair needs between 20 minutes and 2 hours before the operation of Cell1 can be continued and the order can be completed.
If the sensor of manufacturing Cell1 reaches a value above approximately 4, the operation capacity of Cell1 drops and Cell1 needs repair.
Cell2 fails most of the time within the next hour as soon as I have heard a sharp loud noise from the machine in Cell2. I guess the noise is somewhere above 90 decibels.

The AGV fails in rare cases during the unloading and can’t proceed in its operation unless twisted Material2 is removed from the AGV. It could be because a human worker jostled the forks minimally when loading the AGV manually. The AGV loading happens after a new order arrived and before the AGV transports Material2 to Cell2.
If Sensor1 of manufacturing Cell1 reaches a value of probable 4 and Sensor2 a value of above probable 2, the chances are about even that Cell1 needs repair.
Cell2 fails almost certainly within the next hour as soon as there is a sharp loud noise from the machine in Cell2. With a high likelihood the noise is somewhere above 90 decibels.
It is impossible that the AGV continues its operation, if Material2 is delivered twisted from the AGV.
I am certain that if the AGV runs more than 2 months without maintenance, there is the possibility that Cell1 fails and needs repair.
It is very likely that an error in Machine1 occurs, when a noise of probably 90 decibel happens after Machine1 starts up.
I am pretty sure that the AGV fails if the battery is below 25%, as the system accidentally shuts down when only limited energy is available.
The chances are about even that the AGV fails during transport after the step line2_direction and the certain step manual_loading, if screw1 is untight.
Machine2 has a very delicate folding mechanism. If especially material5 arrives a bit twisted it is very likely the folding arms tilt and Machine2 fails.
If the stamp of Machine2 is used longer than 16 days, it is likely that Machine2 produces intermediate products with an error.
If material arrives with a higher core temperature than 60 degree, it is not unlikely that Machine2 will fail within the next hour.
I have to correct myself. I am now certain, that the error in Machine1 occurs, when the pressure jumps above 120 Pascal.
The AGV gets loaded certainly in the step load_manual after the step new_order and before the AGV can start to transport the material.
If Machine1 makes a sharp noise about 70 decibels the chances are about even that Machine1 will fail.

Machine 2 has a very delicate folding mechanism. If especially material 5 arrives a bit twisted it is likely the folding arms tilt and machine 2 fails.
